summary:
The magnetic effect of electric current is an important phenomenon that has many practical applications in our daily lives.

When an electric current flows through a conductor, it produces a magnetic field around it. This phenomenon is known as the magnetic effect of electric current. The magnetic field disappears when the current stops flowing. It is this property of electric currents that allows us to create strong magnets and electromagnets.

The magnetic compass needle deflects towards the pole with which it is brought close to, due to the magnetic field produced by the magnet or the electric current carrying wire. This deflection indicates that the current carrying wire has a magnetic effect on the compass needle. The region around a magnet or a current carrying wire where its magnetic effect can be felt is said to have a magnetic field.

The increase in number of turns of the coil also makes the coil a stronger magnet, as more magnetic material is used. A single cell provides only a small amount of current, so the magnetic field is weak. As a result, the deflection of the compass needle is less and the coil can only attract a few clips. The battery with more cells gives a larger current as compared to that with a single cell, creating a stronger magnetic field.

The magnetic effect of electric current has many practical applications in our daily lives. It is used in devices like electromagnets, electric bells, motors, fans, loudspeakers, and more. These devices rely on the magnetic effect of electric currents to work efficiently. The magnetic compass also relies on this phenomenon to function correctly.

The magnetic field produced by an electric current can be affected by various factors such as the number of turns of the coil, the strength of the battery, and the type of conductor used. Understanding these factors is crucial in designing and building devices that harness the power of electric currents.
